claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has a homogeneous, single-phase fcc solid-solution starting state.
The low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are governed by suppression of a deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Ti changes the local chemical environment in CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti may change magnetic interactions in CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti prevents CoCrFeNiTi from reaching the stacking-fault-energy conditions needed to activate an fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Ti prevents CoCrFeNiTi from reaching the magnetic conditions needed to activate an fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Dislocation glide is the dominant deformation mode in CoCrFeNiTi.
CrCoNi undergoes a deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp phase transformation.
In CrCoNi, the fcc-to-hcp transformation is triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
The deformation-induced transformation in CrCoNi increases strength without compromising plastic deformation.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation hardens related alloys by creating additional barriers to dislocation motion.
Magnetic configuration can control the fcc-hcp energy difference in CrCoNi-related alloys.
CoCrFeNi without Ti is known to undergo a deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
During deformation, CoCrFeNiTi will develop little or no hcp phase and will remain largely fcc.
Deformed CoCrFeNiTi will have a lower work-hardening rate than a comparison alloy that undergoes transformation-induced strengthening.
Suppression of transformation-induced strengthening explains the combination of lower strength and hardening with favorable plasticity in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed mechanism applies to near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi at room temperature under moderate-to-high strain-rate deformation.
Comparable hcp formation and transformation-associated hardening in CoCrFeNiTi would falsify the proposed suppression mechanism.
